claims.content: During correlation of an incoming J2 PPLI report, if no correlation is found, the C2 JU integrates the received J2 PPLI report into its surveillance database as part of the surveillance picture.
During automatic correlation, if local/remote data indicate that the two tracks have an Identity difference that constitutes a conflict, the C2 JU shall not automatically correlate them.
When an ID difference cannot be automatically accepted or rejected, the differences are presented to the operators for evaluation and may require voice coordination for final resolution.

Automatic acceptance of a requested correlation (RV=3) is rejected when: (1) tracks are of different Environment/Category or have an existing E/C conflict; (2) one track is simulated and the other live; or (3) both tracks are locally derived real-time tracks.
Correlation inhibition is not applied when either track has the Strength field set to a value greater than 1, nor is it inhibited when either track has Strength set to No Statement.

If the position or other data in a PPLI meet the system's decorrelation criteria, the PPLI and local track data are decorrelated; afterwards, the PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator field and the PPLI IFF/SIF Indicator field are both reported as No Statement.
If the locally held Environment/Category of a track differs from the Environment/Category received in a J3.X or J7.0 (ACT=1) message for that track, the operator is alerted.
If local data and received data differ regarding whether the Track Number (TN) is assigned to a point or a track, the operator is alerted.

When an Environment/Category conflict is detected upon receipt of a Surveillance message or J7.0 (ACT=1) message with differing air/surface/land classification, the C2 JU processes and resolves the E/C conflict prior to ID conflict resolution; once detected, no further processing to detect an ID conflict occurs.

When a difference report is rejected by an operator action, the information is reported as follows: if the JU has R2, transmit local Environment/Category in a Surveillance report; if no R2, transmit in a J7.0 (ACT=1) message.

When a Platform, Platform Activity, or Specific Type value of 0 (No Statement) is received while a non-zero value is held locally during remote ID change acceptance, this constitutes an exception to the rule requiring retention of received values: the JU shall not retain the received No Statement value for retransmission; because the locally held non-zero value differs from the accepted retransmission value, the JU shall instead report the locally held non-zero value.

When an Air Platform value of 6 (Tanker), 7 (Tanker (Boom Only)), or 8 (Tanker (Drogue Only)) is held locally and a different value is received, operator alert is optional; the system may proceed without alerting.
C2 JU
Two tracks are being reported to the interface, and the C2 JU has recognized that they are eligible for correlation.
A difference report is available for operator action.

The C2 JU has updated the track's identity classification: exercise-involved live tracks are distinguished from other live tracks via Exercise Indicator and Identity Amplifying Descriptor, and Environment/Category differences are resolved.

After successful resolution of Environment/Category differences and determination of Track Number continuity, the C2 JU has transmitted the local Environment/Category in the appropriate Surveillance report if it has R², or in a J7.0 (ACT=1) message if it does not have R².

Track Number continuity has been determined per Table 4.7-1 when the entity type changes: if the E/C change is legal and the original TN is retained, the entity is reported in the appropriate J3.X SURVEILLANCE message with the same TN; if the proposed E/C change is accepted by the R² JU operator, the original TN is dropped via a J7.0 (ACT=0) DROP TRACK message and the entity is reported as a NEW TN in the appropriate J3.X SURVEILLANCE or J5.4 message.
The C2 JU has retained the received values of the Platform, Platform Activity, Specific Type, and Special Interest Indicator fields.

After processing a J7.2 correlation request with RV=3, the C2 JU has automatically accepted the requested correlation only when the following conditions held: the two tracks were not of a different E/C and neither had an existing E/C conflict, one track was not simulated while the other was live, and the two tracks were not both locally derived real-time tracks.

After an Environment/Category change is accepted and the entity is to be reported under a new Track Number, the C2 JU has assigned the new Track Number from its allocated block and holds R² responsibility for that track at the time of assignment.

If automatic correlation was attempted to resolve Track Number continuity, it succeeded only when none of the blocking conditions were present: no ID conflict, no differing Mode II codes with the current local code, not both tracks locally derived real-time, and Strength field ≤1 or No Statement.

The C2 JU enters track identity classification when, as the R² JU, it changes the Environment/Category of a track as specified in section 4.7.1.2.1, resolving the Environment/Category difference, reporting the result in the appropriate Surveillance report if it has R² or in a J7.0 (ACT = 1) message for conflicts if it does not have R², and determining Track Number continuity per Table 4.7-1; the C2 JU also enters when a difference report is rejected by an operator action, reporting the result according to the same R²-based rule; when it recognizes that two tracks being reported to the interface are eligible for correlation, it initiates action to resolve the dual designation; it may elect to automatically accept changes in Environment/Category, Identity, or Exercise Indicator received in a track report with the PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator set to value 1, provided the new identity is Friend and the locally held identity is not Hostile; and when it receives a J7.2 message with the Response Value field set to value 3, it automatically accepts the requested correlation unless one of the prespecified restrictions applies.

The C2 JU commences the correlation process by comparing locally derived sensor data (position, velocity, and altitude) with the data received on the interface, in order to prevent or eliminate dual designations.

The C2 JU verifies that automatic correlation is not blocked by a differing Mode II code with a current local Mode II code, by both tracks being locally derived real-time tracks, or by a track with Strength field greater than 1, and determines that an Identity difference constitutes a conflict.

When the received Surveillance message or J7.0 (ACT=1) message reports a different Environment/Category and ID, the C2 JU processes and resolves the Environment/Category conflict prior to resolving the ID conflict.
The C2 JU resolves any Exercise Indicator conflict prior to resolving the ID or Identity Amplifying Descriptor conflict.
Because the conflicting ID is the only remaining correlation restriction, the C2 JU alerts the operator and presents the allowed resolution actions.
The operator changes the local ID, thereby allowing automatic correlation.
The C2 JU evaluates the Platform, Platform Activity, Specific Type, and Special Interest Indicator fields as part of the identity change and includes the change in a J3.X or J7.0 (ACT=1) message.

The R² JU determines Track Number continuity in accordance with Table 4.7-1: if the original TN is retained, the entity is reported in the appropriate J3.X surveillance message with the same TN; if the Environment/Category change requires a new TN, a J7.0 (ACT = 0) Drop Track message is transmitted for the original TN and the entity is reported with the new TN in the appropriate J3.X surveillance message or J5.4 message.

The use case is triggered when a JU changes the Environment/Category of a track (e.g., Space to air, Air to space/surface/land), or when an operator rejects a difference report. Additionally, a C2 JU may elect to automatically accept changes in Environment/Category, Identity, or Exercise Indicator received in a track report with the PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator set to value 1.

The C2 JU wants to manage track identity classification so that exercise-involved live tracks are distinguished from other live tracks being reported, and Environment/Category differences are resolved and Track Number continuity is determined when an entity type changes.

scope_contract.goal_statement: The C2 JU wants to manage track identity classification so that exercise-involved live tracks are distinguished from other live tracks being reported, and Environment/Category differences are resolved and Track Number continuity is determined when an entity type changes.
scope_contract.canonical_success_scenario: One canonical successful instance is the C2 JU classifying a reported live track's identity by distinguishing whether it is exercise-involved, resolving any Environment/Category differences, and determining Track Number continuity when the entity type changes.
scope_contract.start_boundary: The C2 JU is handling a live track whose identity classification needs to be managed (exercise status, Environment/Category, or Track Number continuity).
scope_contract.success_boundary: The track's identity classification is updated such that exercise-involved live tracks are distinguished from other live tracks, Environment/Category differences are resolved, and Track Number continuity has been determined.
in_scope_actions: Distinguishing exercise-involved live tracks from other live tracks
Determining Track Number continuity when an entity type changes
excluded_adjacent_actions: Assuming or transferring R2 for an Interface Unit
Post-classification transmission/inhibition of tracks via ENV/ID/GEO/SP filters
variant_dimensions: Exercise status classification (exercise-involved versus other live tracks)
Track Number continuity outcome when entity type changes

claims.content: Diverges from Step 4. The C2 JU may elect to automatically accept changes in Environment/Category, Identity, or Exercise Indicator received in a track report with the PPLI Track Number and Identity Indicator set to value 1, provided the new identity is Friend and the locally held identity is not Hostile.
Diverges from Step 4. If an Environment/Category conflict is detected during processing of a received message, the C2 JU need not perform further processing to detect an ID conflict.
Diverges from Step 5. When the Exercise Indicator is set to 0 (Non-Exercise Track), the C2 JU specifies the standard identity of the track in the Identity field.

Diverges from Step 5. When the Exercise Indicator is set to 1, the C2 JU considers data concerning the track to be artificial for exercise purposes, except for the non-artificial fields: Track Number, Tracking Data, Simulation Indicator, Environment/Category, Status Data on Air Tracks, and Status Data on Surface (Maritime) Tracks.

Diverges from Step 6. If the receiving C2 JU does not have R² for the Track Number and no local positional data is held, the C2 JU automatically accepts the received ID data and places the remote ID in the database for retention.
Diverges from Step 7. Instead of changing the local ID only, the operator may change the local Exercise Indicator and ID, thereby allowing automatic correlation.
Diverges from Step 7. The operator transmits an ID Difference Report; automatic correlation is allowed if the remote ID or Exercise Indicator and ID is changed.
Diverges from Step 8. Difference resolution of the Platform, Platform Activity, Specific Type, and Special Interest Indicator field values is not mandatory.
Diverges from Step 8. When an Air Platform value of 6 (Tanker), 7 (Tanker (Boom Only)), or 8 (Tanker (Drogue Only)) is held locally and a different value is received, operator alert is optional.

missing_aspects: Track Number continuity outcome when entity type changes (retain original TN vs assign new TN) has no evidence-supported alternative branch in the supplied pool; it is covered only in postconditions.

quality_flags.detail: [goal_mainflow_alignment] The goal statement lists three distinct outcomes: distinguishing exercise-involved live tracks from other live tracks, resolving Environment/Category differences, and determining Track Number continuity when an entity type changes. Main flow covers E/C conflict priority (step 4), Exercise Indicator conflict priority (step 5), and ID-conflict-driven correlation resolution (steps 6-8), but no main_flow step determines Track Number continuity when an entity type changes. The goal is therefore broader than the main flow and appears to conflate multiple use cases/actions into one goal. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (C2 JU as the acting stakeholder is not supported by the cited evidence cards.))

[mainflow_trigger_continuity] The Trigger is a set of operator/C2 JU actions (E/C change, difference-report rejection, auto-accept of E/C/ID/Exercise Indicator changes), but Main Flow step 1 restarts from the Precondition state - recognizing that two tracks are eligible for correlation and initiating dual-designation resolution. None of the Trigger variants is actually continued by step 1, so the main flow reads as a different scenario. (atomic grounding: candidate remains incomplete (No cited evidence supports the added detail that a C2 JU resolves the resulting identity classification conflict.))

[mainflow_trigger_continuity] The Trigger claim lists only Environment/Category change, difference-report rejection, and track-report auto-accept as initiators. Main Flow step 1 additionally enters the use case when the C2 JU recognizes that two reported tracks are eligible for correlation and when it receives a J7.2 message with Response Value field set to 3. These are distinct trigger events in the main flow but are absent from the Trigger slot, so the main flow does not continue from a complete and accurate trigger definition.

inconsistency_hints: The Trigger includes 'when an operator rejects a difference report'. Rejecting a difference report requires that a difference report has already been generated and is pending, but the Preconditions only state that two tracks are reported and recognized as eligible for correlation; no difference-report state is asserted.

Postcondition 3 requires Track Number continuity to be determined per Table 4.7-1, including retaining the original TN, dropping it via J7.0 (ACT=0), and reporting a NEW TN. The Main Flow contains no step that decides TN continuity, drops a track, or reports a NEW TN; its final J3.X/J7.0 (ACT=1) message step does not cover the ACT=0/new-TN branch.

Exception flow claim 11 (EC-EF-012) states that a received Platform/Platform Activity/Specific Type value of 0 with a non-zero local value is 'an exception to the rule requiring retention of received values during remote ID change acceptance', but it does not specify the resulting behavior or outcome. It leaves unclear whether the local value is retained, the received No Statement is ignored/discarded, an alert is raised, or the flow returns to another step.

Postcondition 5 requires filter-based transmission inhibition for Simulation-status tracks, but the Main Flow never addresses Simulation status, ENV/ID/GEO/SP filters, or inhibition. The goal scope contract explicitly excludes post-classification transmission/inhibition via filters, so this postcondition is out of scope and unreachable.

Postcondition 6 asserts Track Number assignment and R² responsibility for every initiated/reported track/point, but the Main Flow does not include any TN-allocation or R²-responsibility step. This broader track-management obligation is not reached by the identity-classification flow shown.

Precondition 2 uses a completed trigger event as a required prior state: it says a difference report 'has been rejected by an operator action,' while the trigger is 'when an operator rejects a difference report.' For the trigger to be meaningful, the report must be pending, not already rejected; otherwise the trigger action cannot occur. It also makes a branch-specific event a mandatory precondition for all trigger paths.

The trigger identifies three distinct entry events, but the main_flow does not continue from any of them. Step 1 restarts from the correlation-eligibility precondition ('two tracks ... eligible for correlation'), and the following steps only implement a manual correlation/identity-conflict resolution. The operator-rejected difference-report branch and the track-report autoaccept branch are absent; consequently, postcondition 5 (J7.2 RV=3 automatic acceptance) has no path to be reached.
